results.note: UncorroboratedDefinition (registry.py:37-42) is a plain optional field on IndicatorDefinition (line 60), defaulting to None with no computed/inferred logic anywhere in the class. tests/test_uncorroborated.py:31-42 loads an entry that explicitly sets uncorroborated.note and asserts corroboration is None while uncorroborated carries the exact note text — confirms the flag is only ever set by explicit YAML.

Test model_dumps a corroborated and an uncorroborated IndicatorDefinition and asserts the dicts differ, with each carrying the opposite field populated/None (lines 53-68) — real, non-vacuous assertions. This story's declared touched files are registry.yaml/registry.py/tests only (per US-306-uncorroborated.md), so 'stored data' here is the registry model, not the corroborations DB table; ingest/corroborate.py has zero references to `uncorroborated` (confirmed by grep), so the distinction does not yet reach the actual datapoint/corroboration write path. Since the AC's method is 'test' and the named test matches verbatim and passes with genuine assertions, the criterion as written is satisfied.

load_registry (registry.py:174-188) raises ValueError when has_second_source == is_uncorroborated, i.e. both false (silence) or both true — the same XOR discipline as reject_wildcards on definable_for (lines 62-69). Test at line 71 strips the uncorroborated block and asserts ValueError with matching message 'corroboration declaration'.

assert_registry_coverage (registry.py:191-215) appends a failure when has_second_source == is_uncorroborated (lines 201-206), extending the existing PRD-002 coverage mechanism rather than a new hand-kept list. Test at line 88 constructs a definition with neither field set and asserts AssertionError matching 'corroboration declaration'.

Deterministic gate `uv run python -m ingest.registry --validate` exited 0 (given). Confirmed by reading the shipped ingest/registry.yaml: its sole entry (btc_daily_close) declares corroboration and not uncorroborated, so has_second_source=True/is_uncorroborated=False are unequal and load_registry's new check does not raise.

note: All five criteria are backed by real, assertion-bearing named tests in tests/test_uncorroborated.py that match the story's declared AC test names verbatim, exercising genuine registry.py logic (explicit-only optional field, XOR validation in both load_registry and assert_registry_coverage). One honest scope caveat on C2: the uncorroborated field is a registry/YAML-level declaration only — ingest/corroborate.py, the module that writes actual datapoint/corroboration rows, never references it (zero grep hits outside registry.py/registry.yaml/tests), so the distinction is proven at the registry-model level, not the corroborations-table level. This does not fail the criterion since the story's declared touched files are registry.yaml/registry.py/tests only and the named test is the literal contract. Also note the registry.yaml still ships only the original btc_daily_close entry; the Coin Metrics MVRV example with the upstream-consolidation note exists only inside the test file's synthetic fixture, not as a real shipped indicator — this is consistent with the story's scope (mechanism + validation) but the narrative framing about MVRV itself is illustrative, not literally deployed.
